title: How can we square a number close to a round one?
description: A square is found by turning the rule for a sum times a take away round, so the number is split as the round number and the gap. The board shows two hundred times one hundred ninety four, and then the gap squared is added. Keeko wants to stop after the multiplication, and a small case with ten shows what goes missing.
teaching_notes: One idea: use eigh squared equals eigh plus b times eigh minus b, plus b squared, choosing b so that eigh plus b is a round number. Watch for students who stop after the multiplication and forget to add b squared.

source: Use a² = (a + b)(a − b) + b² to find 197².
video_script.why: The child knows a sum times a take away, but has not yet turned the rule round to square a number near a round one.
video_script.substitution: Take a as the number, choose b so that a plus b is round, multiply the two brackets and add b squared.
video_script.anchor: the book's rule for squaring a number, with the number one hundred ninety seven
video_script.wrong_answer: stop at thirty eight thousand eight hundred
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies two hundred by one hundred ninety four and stops at thirty eight thousand eight hundred. The rule also adds b squared, so nine is missing.
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred ninety seven squared is thirty eight thousand eight hundred nine.

final_answer.spoken: thirty eight thousand eight hundred nine

names.{{NAME_7}}: the Indian mathematician who gave a quick way to find squares

maths_rules: a² = (a + b)(a − b) + b², because (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²
a = 197 and b = 3: a + b = 200 and a − b = 194
small case: a = 10 and b = 1: 11 × 9 = 99, and 99 + 1² = 100 = 10²
video_script.design: One idea: reach a round number, multiply the two brackets, then add b squared. The rule card stays through the idea part. Keeko's wrong idea is to stop after the multiplication.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we find one hundred ninety seven squared without long multiplication?

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Your book turns the last rule round. Eigh squared is eigh plus b times eigh minus b, plus b squared.
<bookmark mark='why'/>It is true because eigh plus b times eigh minus b is eigh squared minus b squared.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Adding b squared to both sides gives eigh squared back.

beats.on_screen: Given: the number 197, to be squared
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number one hundred ninety seven, to be squared.

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find one hundred ninety seven squared using the rule.
<bookmark mark='choose'/>Step one, take eigh as one hundred ninety seven.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Choose b as three, so that eigh plus b is the round number two hundred.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Then eigh minus b is one hundred ninety four.

marks.put: the values are put into the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step two, put the values in the rule.
<bookmark mark='line'/>One hundred ninety seven squared is two hundred times one hundred ninety four, plus three squared.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Step three, multiply the two brackets. Two hundred times one hundred ninety four is twice one hundred ninety four, times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='hundred'/>Twice one hundred ninety four is three hundred eighty eight. Times one hundred, that gives thirty eight thousand eight hundred.

beats.on_screen: 3² = 9; then 38800 + 9 waits to be worked out

marks.add: 38800 + 9 is written, not yet worked out

beats.colours: the b² term in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Step four, three squared is nine.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Then we add nine to thirty eight thousand eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>One hundred ninety seven squared is thirty eight thousand eight hundred nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we can stop at thirty eight thousand eight hundred, after the multiplication.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Let us try a small case. Take eigh as ten and b as one.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Eleven times nine is ninety nine, but ten squared is one hundred.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>One is missing, and that is b squared. The last part of the rule must be added.
